//: VARIANT of the built-in `applepcc` lane, for when the defaults don't fit — a different
//1: port, a Unix socket, or an OpenAI-compatible server that isn't `fm serve` at all.
//2: If you just want PCC on the default setup you do NOT need this file: export
//4: STARTING THE SERVER — you do not have to type this yourself; run it from anywhere:
//5: osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to do script "fm serve --port 1976"'
//6: `fm` gates PCC by walking the caller's ancestry to the session boundary and checking that
//7: ancestor's code signature, so a server cli-bridge spawns itself is refused ('PCC inference
//8: is not available in this context'). Asking Terminal.app to start it makes Terminal the
//9: parent — the same trusted chain as a human typing it. Verified A/B from one clean state:
//9a: direct spawn (parent launchd) -> pcc available:false; via Terminal (parent -zsh) -> true.
//9b: Check it yourself with: curl -s localhost:1976/health
//10: Keyless by design: no --key-env is passed, so the bundled bridge sends no auth header.
//11: Same recipe works for llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio's server — swap the base URL.
//12: model_flag emits `--model <id>` on its own — don't repeat it in `ask` or it lands twice.
install_hint: start `fm serve --port 1976` yourself, then export APPLE_FM_SERVE_URL=1 to unhide this lane
note: Apple Private Cloud Compute over HTTP, through an `fm serve` you started. model=pcc (server-side, bigger, metered quota) or system (on-device, unmetered). Private either way — PCC is stateless.
